html:
Nader Shah was a soldier from the Afshar tribe of Khorasan who rose to rule Iran from 1736 to 1747. He founded the Afsharid dynasty and was one of the strongest rulers in Iranian history.

When Safavid power collapsed after the Afghan capture of Isfahan in 1722, Nader served a Safavid prince as general. He drove out the Afghans, pushed back the Ottomans and the Russians, and then set the last Safavids aside and took the crown himself.

  • In 1739 he invaded the Mughal Empire, beat its army at Karnal and sacked Delhi.
  • He carried home the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond, a blow from which Mughal prestige never recovered.
  • He fought on in the Caucasus and Central Asia and built up a navy in the Gulf.

His rule grew harsh and suspicious, and his taxes ruined much of the country. His own officers murdered him in 1747. His empire broke up quickly; one of his commanders, Ahmad Shah Durrani, founded the state that became Afghanistan.
